name: Penrith Forge

location.about: An iron town of about 90,000 at the foot of the fells: the forges and rolling mills that made rails for half the world, and the railway that took them away. Champions of England four times before 1933 - the first great northern club.

colours.story: Iron grey and red - the colour of the forge's iron and of its fire. The workers who started the club in 1879 wore their grey work shirts with a red sash.

home.shirt: iron grey with a red sash

third.shirt: white with a thin red and grey sash

rivals.why: the 1896 title race, and two cup finals (1981 and 1990) - Penrith won all three
1929, when Penrith beat them to the title, and the 2017 Founders' Cup final, when Penrith did it again

history.title: The first great northern club
history.text: Founded in 1879 by men from the forge. Champions in 1890 (ahead of Ashvale), second in 1893, champions again in 1896 (ahead of Bramhall); beaten in the 1899 Founders' Cup final.

history.title: Two more titles, then the slump
history.text: Beaten in the 1910 Founders' Cup final; relegated, back as Second Division champions in 1925 - and champions twice more, 1929 (ahead of Northwick) and 1932 (ahead of Harrowby). Then the forge closed in the slump, the best players were sold to pay the bills, and the club fell apart: 0-9 at Castleford, 1-11 at Whitcombe, 1-10 at Kingsmere, and relegation.

history.title: Hard years
history.text: Beaten Founders' Cup finalists two years running, 1954 and 1955 (against Brackenfield); Second Division champions in 1968. The town lost its works one by one; the club hung on.

history.title: The cup years
history.text: The Founders' Cup in 1975 (against Wrexford) and 1981 (Bramhall), the Charter Cup in 1979 and 1990 (Bramhall again); beaten in the 1992 Founders' Cup final. Relegated, and back as Second Division champions in 1999.

history.title: Up the hill again
history.text: Beaten in the 2010 Charter Cup final; the Founders' Cup in 2017 against Northwick. Down, up through the play-offs in 2020, down again - and back as Division 1 runners-up in 2025.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1890 = 1889-90).

legends.name: Isaac Teasdale
legends.note: A forge hand; captain of the 1890 champions.

legends.name: Joe Graham
legends.note: Two Founders' Cups and two Charter Cups.

records.attendance: 44,612 v Bramhall Borough, Founders' Cup sixth round, 1955 (Hammerfield, before seating)

badge.about: An anvil and the fells behind it; four stars for the four titles. Motto 'Igne Fortior' - stronger for the fire.
badge.design: An iron-grey shield with a red border. In the centre a black anvil with red sparks flying from it; behind it three grey fell summits against a red sky. Four small red stars above the shield; 'PENRITH FORGE' on a red ribbon below.

ground.name: Hammerfield

stands.name: Forge Stand
stands.features: the main stand, on the site of the old forge offices: tunnel, dugouts, the four title pennants

stands.name: Hammer End
stands.features: the home end - a big old steam hammer stands outside it as a memorial

stands.name: Fell Stand
stands.features: a long single tier with the fells rising behind it

stands.name: Railway End
stands.features: away fans; beside the railway line

ground.surroundings: green fells rising behind the east stand, the empty brick sheds of the old forge, a steam hammer kept as a memorial, the main railway line and red sandstone terraced houses
ground.atmosphere: small, hard and proud - the fells echo the Hammer End's songs
